facts.F24: No model for the nav membership, visibility and Home-removal claims: there is no shared state, no multi-step protocol, no concurrency and no crash window - each claim is one synchronous render of one template from one already-resolved NavContext, and the rights domain is the closed four-member set (plain member, workspace admin, instance admin, both) that the shipped icon-rail outline already enumerates. The claims are therefore finite and exhausted by enumerated cases, not by a state model. Quint is installed on this host, so this is a reasoned modelling choice and not a tooling gap; Agda is absent and no claim here needs a proof over types.
facts.F25: The three new items carry no aria-current and NavSection keeps its two variants (Home, Board). Home therefore stays the single marked section on /teams, /workspace/invites and /admin/tokens exactly as it already is on /account/settings and /keyboard-help, so "exactly one primary navigation item is marked as the current page" (navigation-bar-linear-ui, notification-preferences-ui) keeps holding with five primary members instead of two.
facts.F26: The stylesheet is not touched. The three items reuse .sidebar__item, .sidebar__icon and .sidebar__label, and both the desk collapsed rules and the max-width 480px block already make .sidebar__nav and .sidebar__user wrapping rows bounded by the bar (flex-wrap: wrap with min-width: 0), which is quantified over members and not over a member count. foundry.fb3aa227.css is content-hash named, so any byte change migrates templates/base.html, static/VENDOR.md and three hashed-name assertions in crates/foundry-app/src/lib.rs; spending that for rules that need no change is refused. The .actions rules become unreferenced and stay in place until the next stylesheet change re-fingerprints the file.
facts.F27: Subtraction the removal makes available: DashboardRoot drops is_instance_admin, is_workspace_admin and csrf. Once the Quick actions list is gone those three fields have no reader, and the same three facts already reach the page through the nav field. The handler keeps computing all three, unchanged and fail-closed, because NavContext::for_page consumes them.
facts.F28: Glyphs come from the release static/VENDOR.md already pins, lucide-static 1.75.0 (ISC): users for Teams, user-plus for Invite a member, key-round for Machine tokens. The shape children of package/icons/<name>.svg are copied verbatim in upstream order; the svg wrapper is authored like the seven shipped ones (class sidebar__icon, aria-hidden true, focusable false, no title element, stroke currentColor, no fill or colour literal). VENDOR.md gains the three names and its "all seven" count becomes ten.
facts.F29: Placement inside nav#sidebar-nav is load-bearing, not cosmetic: the collapse control reaches the nav by aria-controls="sidebar-nav", the collapsed rules select [data-nav-collapsed] .sidebar__nav, and the browser rail reading enumerates ".sidebar a.sidebar__item" plus the sign-out button. An item added inside that element is therefore folded, clipped, revealed and read with no change to static/js/nav-collapse.js and no change to crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/rail_reading.rs.

facts.F30: P4 is inherited, not re-oracled. The shipped nav-collapse-icon-rail scenarios quantify over the members they read from the live document, so the enlarged set is covered by RE-RUNNING that lane rather than by a new browser scenario. The slice therefore takes its RED from fast served-markup scenarios, and the close must name the browser lane that actually ran: on a host without Docker that lane observes nothing and P4 stays unverified behind a green gate.
facts.F31: No stored or validated input is added: the three destinations are fixed href literals /teams, /workspace/invites and /admin/tokens with no path or query parameter, so no length, range or character bound applies to this change and none is invented.
